budget_items.what_was_said: The applicant cited soaring construction costs, labor shortages and vehicle inventory as reasons for delaying construction.
Plastic chamber materials were expensive and hard to obtain, so a concrete galley system was proposed instead.
A member noted that preparing plans on a known datum would be an additional bill to the client.
The board discussed waiving peer review, which carries a fee, since no hydrology or engineering was changing.
A resident said a successful restaurant brings the town more sales tax income.

minutes.headline: Planning Board extended North End Subaru's approval a year and kept the El Forno hearing open to June 27.
minutes.summary: The three-member Planning Board extended North End Subaru's site plan approval by one year. It approved a de minimis change at the Lunenburg Central project on Shirley Road. It spent most of the evening on the El Forno site plan for a permanent outdoor seating structure, waiving several submission items and the peer review, then continued the hearing to June 27 so a plan showing setbacks can be added. Neighbor parking concerns were heard; the board said the Select Board controls parking prohibitions.

what_happened.line: The Planning Board continued the El Forno site plan hearing for a permanent outdoor seating structure at 494 Electric Avenue to June 27, keeping it open.
Before continuing, the board waived several El Forno submission items, the peer review and the datum requirement, and asked for a plan showing setbacks.
The board extended North End Subaru's site plan approval by one year, to July 13, 2023.
The board accepted a de minimis change at the Lunenburg Central project, 535 Shirley Road, a concrete galley system and curtain drain replacing plastic chambers.
A Pierce Avenue neighbor objected to restaurant parking on the residential street; the board said parking prohibitions go through the Select Board.

why_it_matters: The El Forno decision is still open, so neighbors on Pierce Avenue and other residents can still weigh in on the building and its parking before the board closes the hearing.
Waiving peer review and several plan documents means the El Forno approval will rest on the applicant's own plans rather than an independent engineering review.
